dish: Pork-bone (tonkotsu) Okinawa soba topped with three meats; 'Jirō-style' mashi-mashi sōmen piled with bean sprouts and cabbage
n: Okinawa Soba Kintarō, Nanjō (沖縄そば 金太郎)
w: A local soba shop in Tamagusuku-Funakoshi known for a rich pork-bone soup and huge 'Jirō-inspired' bowls heaped with vegetables, with a three-meat Okinawa soba as its standard. Its owner chairs the Nanjō Okinawa-soba stamp rally promoting the city as a soba town.

dish: Kuruma-ebi soba — Okinawa soba with four Kume-jima kuruma prawns in a broth enriched with prawn paste and Kume-jima miso
n: Yukui-dokoro Washima, Kume Island (ゆくい処 笑島)
w: Kume-jima's kuruma-prawn soba, built on an Okinawa-soba dashi with a paste of the island's farmed kuruma prawns and local miso, won the grand prix at the 'Nippon no Takaramono' world competition held in Singapore. The shop sells around 60 bowls a day and often sells out.

dish: Mozuku soba — Okinawa soba noodles kneaded with the shop's own Zamami-farmed thick mozuku seaweed
w: A mozuku farmer's own restaurant three minutes' walk from Zamami port, serving soba made with thick mozuku grown in the Kerama sea; Okinawa Times praised the firm noodles' match with the seaweed's texture. It also sells its mozuku and runs snorkel tours.
